policy_title: Protect and restore 30% of land and seas for nature by 2030
stated: Plan to give 30% of land and sea back to nature by 2030, ensuring permanent protection. Prioritise re-wetting peatland, increasing unharvested forest and woodland by over 50%, and create new protected spaces in urban settings. Make at least 30% of UK domestic waters fully protected Marine Protected Areas, banning destructive fishing practices.

source.quote: We would plan to give 30% of land and sea back to nature by 2030 ensuring that it is permanently protected. A priority would be the re-wetting of all peatland and increasing unharvested forest and woodland by over 50%. Elected Greens also commit to making at least 30% of UK domestic waters into fully protected marine protected areas by 2030. We will seek to ban all destructive fishing practices from Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) and other domestic waters.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets emissions (peatland re-wetting sequesters carbon), water quality (marine protected areas, ban on destructive fishing), and nature/biodiversity across 30% of UK land and sea — a core, non-negligible environmental policy.

Banning destructive fishing practices across 30% of UK domestic waters directly restricts access to fishing grounds for commercial and coastal fishers, with a concrete mechanism: reduced catch opportunity → lower incomes and job losses in fishing-dependent communities, moving employment rate and real wages for that sector.

Banning destructive fishing across 30% of UK waters and converting significant land to protected/unharvested status imposes near-term productivity costs on fishing and land-based sectors, while long-run ecosystem services (pollination, flood regulation, carbon credits, fisheries recovery) are a concrete economic counterweight — a genuine dual-horizon tradeoff affecting real living standards and economic opportunity.

Achieving 30x30 requires substantial public expenditure (land acquisition or ecosystem-service payments to landowners, MPA enforcement, peatland restoration works, compensation to displaced fishers); without a stated funding mechanism, this is a material unfunded or partially-funded commitment that plausibly moves the debt-path/funded-vs-borrowed indicator.

membership_note: Three fundamentals clear the non-negligible bar: O6 is the direct target; O13 captures the dual-horizon economic tradeoff (near-term sector costs vs long-term natural capital gains); O12 captures the fiscal commitment implicit in large-scale habitat protection and MPA enforcement. Food-price effects on O2 and fishing/farming employment effects on O4 are real but likely negligible at the macro scale given import substitution and sector size.
